  FINISHED AGENDA & MINUTES

CALL TO ORDER

At 7:57 a.m. the meeting was called to order. Chair Sanders presiding.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present: Sanders, Schwerin, St Bernard, Betancourt, Curtis, Girgis, Lesen, Red
Eagle, Clark, Van Meeveren

Commissioners Absent: Gupta, McNeeley, Tejani, Vaias, Walton

Also present: Anissa Davis, City Health Officer, Jessica Schumer, Deputy Director, Dennis Keith,
Executive Assistant, Alison King, Director of Health .

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  24-53244  Recommendation to approve the minutes of the Board of Health and Human
  Services meeting held Friday, April 12, 2024.

  A motion was made by Member Lesen, seconded by Member St Bernard, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  10 Sanders, Schwerin, St Bernard, Betancourt, Curtis, Girgis, Lesen,
  Red Eagle, Clark, Van Meeveren
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 5 Gupta, McNeeley, Tejani, Vaias, Walton

2.  24-53245  Recommendation to receive and file a report from the Director of Health and
  Human Services.

  Alison King, Director of Health and Human Services, provided the following
  information to the Board:
  • Informed the Board that she will be meeting with the Health Directors of Los

  Page 1 of 4
   BOARD OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES MINUTES
  FRIDAY, MAY 10, 2024
  3861 WORSHAM AVENUE

  Angeles County and the City of Pasadena.
  • The Department is still engaged in the 2025 Budget process and discussions
  are ongoing.
  • There will be some staffing changes in the Department due to the loss of
  COVID/Recovery Act funding. Currently the City has a 20% vacancy rate
  and affected staff, where possible, will be transitioned to fill some of these
  vacant positions.
  • The City Council voted to go dark during the month of July; therefore, there
  will be no Council meetings held that month.
  • The Mayor announced this week as Housing Innovation Week.
  • On May 7th, the City Council officially ratified the declaration of a Public
  Health Emergency regarding a local TB Outbreak. Department staff are
  currently working with staff from the California Department of Public Health
  (CDPH) and the Centers for Disease Control (CDC).
  • The City released the results of the 2024 Homeless Count which show a 2%
  decrease in homelessness in Long Beach.

  A motion was made by Vice Chair Schwerin, seconded by Member Lesen, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  10 Sanders, Schwerin, St Bernard, Betancourt, Curtis, Girgis, Lesen,
  Red Eagle, Clark, Van Meeveren
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 5 Gupta, McNeeley, Tejani, Vaias, Walton

3.  24-53246  Recommendation to receive and file a report from the City Health Officer.

  Dr. Anissa Davis, City Health Officer, provided the Board with a brief update on the
  local TB outbreak. California Department of Public Health (CDPH) and Centers for
  Disease Control (CDC) staff are currently on site assisting Department staff with
  contact tracing and investigations. The City declared a public health emergency
  which provides the City with an opportunity to obtain assistance and funding to
  address the outbreak. The threat to the community at-large is extremely low.

  A motion was made by Member St Bernard, seconded by Vice Chair
  Schwerin, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  10 Sanders, Schwerin, St Bernard, Betancourt, Curtis, Girgis, Lesen,
  Red Eagle, Clark, Van Meeveren
  No:  0 None

4.  24-53247  Recommendation to receive and file an update on the City’s Legislative Agenda.

  Dr. Jessica Schumer, Deputy Director, provided the Board with a brief update on
  the State budget. Currently the State is predicting a budget deficit of between
  $38 and $73 Billion. As it is an election year, no tax increases have been
  proposed.

  A motion was made by Member Lesen, seconded by Vice Chair Schwerin, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  10 Sanders, Schwerin, St Bernard, Betancourt, Curtis, Girgis, Lesen,
  Red Eagle, Clark, Van Meeveren
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 5 Gupta, McNeeley, Tejani, Vaias, Walton

5.  24-53248  Recommendation to discuss Board goals and infrastructure.

  Currently the Board is awaiting the findings and recommendations from Mr. James
  Suazo, Executive Director of Long Beach Forward, who facilitated a series of
  strategic planing exercises with the Board. Once Mr. Suazo’s recommendations
  have been received, the Board’s Goals and Infrastructure Subcommittee will meet
  to discuss them and bring a report back to the rest of the Board at a future meeting.

  Chair Sanders briefly discussed that Board members Curtis and St. Bernard will be
  completing their final term on the Board this June. She requested that they reach
  out to any qualified individuals they may know and encourage them to submit an
  application to the Mayor’s office to fill their vacant positions. It was also requested
  that the Department reach out to the Mayor’s office to see if any qualified
  candidates had already applied.

  The Board discussed following the City Council’s lead and also going dark during
  the month of July to accommodate Board member vacation schedules. The Board
  motioned to cancel the July 12, 2024 Board of Health and Human Services
  meeting.

  A motion was made by Member Girgis, seconded by Member Clark, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  10 Sanders, Schwerin, St Bernard, Betancourt, Curtis, Girgis, Lesen,

PUBLIC COMMENT

There was no public comment.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

 Board member St. Bernard provided the Board with a draft copy of a letter of recommendation to the
Mayor and Council regarding permanent beach water quality signage to be installed along
recreational water areas.

 Dr. Jessica Schumer announced that she was in negotiations for a position with the State of
California Department of Public Health. Should negotiations be favorable, she could start her new
position with the State as early as July.

ADJOURNMENT

At 9:04 a.m. the meeting was adjourned.
